chunks: And Zurārah narrated from one of the two of them, عليهما السلام, who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made ruku' and sujud obligatory, while recitation is a sunnah. So whoever leaves the recitation deliberately must repeat the salat, and whoever forgets, then there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الرُّكُوعَ: bowing in salat as an obligatory act
key_terms.السُّجُودَ: prostration in salat as an obligatory act
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a legislated practice that is not treated here as an obligatory pillar
key_terms.فَرَضَ: made obligatory; established as a required duty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets or intentionally leaves the recitation in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a ruling concerning forgetfulness in salat: ruku' and sujud are obligatory components, while recitation is treated as sunnah in this context. If recitation is omitted deliberately, the prayer must be repeated, but if it is omitted out of forgetfulness, no liability is incurred.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1005 – Zurarah narrated from one of the Imams that He said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, has made ruku' (bowing) and Sujood (prostration) obligatory, while recitation is a Sunnah. Whoever intentionally leaves out the recitation must repeat the prayer, but if someone forgets, there is no fault upon them."
